sections.heading: Learning Point 1
sections.content: 167 Our Cultural Heritage and Knowledge Traditions 8 – How the Land Becomes Sacred How the Land Becomes Sacred CHAPTER 8 Ether, air, fire, water, earth, planets, all creatures, directions, trees and plants, rivers and seas, are organs of the supreme Lord’s body. – Bhāgavata Purāṇa 1.

sections.heading: Learning Point 2
sections.content: How do sacred sites and pilgrimage networks connect with the life and culture of the people?

sections.heading: Learning Point 3
sections.content: What role did sacred geography play in the cultural integration of the Indian Subcontinent?

sections.content: Can you name similar places found in your neighbourhood?

sections.heading: Learning Point 6
sections.content: In the limited context of this chapter, sacredness is finding something of deep religious or spiritual significance, worthy of respect and reverence, holy or divine.
sections.source_evidence: In the limited context of this chapter, sacredness is finding something of deep religious or spiritual significance, worthy of respect and reverence, holy or divine.

sections.heading: Learning Point 7
sections.content: It can be a special location or shrine that evokes such deep feelings, high thoughts or emotions.
sections.source_evidence: It can be a special location or shrine that evokes such deep feelings, high thoughts or emotions.

sections.heading: Learning Point 8
sections.content: It can also be, as we will see in this chapter, a journey of a special kind (often called a ‘pilgrimage’), the route the journey takes, or even the very land covered.
sections.source_evidence: It can also be, as we will see in this chapter, a journey of a special kind (often called a ‘pilgrimage’), the route the journey takes, or even the very land covered.

sections.heading: Learning Point 9
sections.content: Sacredness, therefore, is not just connected with religion and spirituality, but also with geography, all sorts of traditions, and, in the case of India, with something more that we will discover soon.
sections.source_evidence: Sacredness, therefore, is not just connected with religion and spirituality, but also with geography, all sorts of traditions, and, in the case of India, with something more that we will discover soon.

sections.heading: Learning Point 10
sections.content: You will find that almost every school of thought and religion in India has its own sacred places.
sections.source_evidence: You will find that almost every school of thought and religion in India has its own sacred places.

sections.heading: Learning Point 11
sections.content: 169 Our Cultural Heritage and Knowledge Traditions 8 – How the Land Becomes Sacred The places in these pictures are revered by followers of Islam, Christianity, Judaism and Zoroastrianism — religions that originated outside India.

sections.heading: Learning Point 12
sections.content: People visit or congregate in these places for prayer and worship.
sections.source_evidence: People visit or congregate in these places for prayer and worship.

sections.heading: Learning Point 13
sections.content: Followers from other faiths also visit them, as can be seen at the Dargah Sharif of Ajmer (Rajasthan) or the Velankanni Church in Tamil Nadu.
sections.source_evidence: Followers from other faiths also visit them, as can be seen at the Dargah Sharif of Ajmer (Rajasthan) or the Velankanni Church in Tamil Nadu.

sections.heading: Learning Point 14
sections.content: People go on pilgrimages to these shrines on special occasions.
sections.source_evidence: People go on pilgrimages to these shrines on special occasions.

sections.heading: Learning Point 15
sections.content: Naturally, when we turn to religions that originated in India, we find that they have many more sacred sites.
sections.source_evidence: Naturally, when we turn to religions that originated in India, we find that they have many more sacred sites.

sections.heading: Learning Point 16
sections.content: In the case of Buddhism, those are often places that were visited by the Buddha or where his relics are kept.
sections.source_evidence: In the case of Buddhism, those are often places that were visited by the Buddha or where his relics are kept.

sections.heading: Learning Point 17
sections.content: Among them is the Great Stūpa at Sanchi (Madhya Pradesh), which is a relic stūpa (you saw this in the chapter on ‘The Rise of Empires’), and the Mahabodhi Stūpa in Bodh Gaya (Bihar), where, according to Buddhist tradition, the Buddha attained enlightenment.

sections.heading: Learning Point 18
sections.content: They are important sites for pilgrims; Bodh Gaya, for instance, receives more than four million visitors every year.
